domain_setting: A modern workplace: an office, a team floor, hiring desk, training area, and career progression path.
recurring_scale_anchors: adult worker busts centered near x=152, with shoulder line around y=128
office desks and counters sit around y=142 with a clear foreground floor at y=154
door, desk chair, folder, laptop, calendar blocks, and tool trays are recurring workplace props
all essential silhouettes stay within x=24..280 and y=16..176 on a 304x192 stage

polysemy_resolution_table.bottom of the career ladder: lowest entry level of a professional career; not a literal household ladder
polysemy_resolution_table.career path: a person's progression through jobs and increasing responsibility; not a road trip
polysemy_resolution_table.dead-end job: a job with no realistic advancement; not a physical dead end or road
polysemy_resolution_table.get ahead: make career progress; not move physically in front of someone
polysemy_resolution_table.hold a position: retain or occupy a role at work; not a body posture or sports position
polysemy_resolution_table.promote: advance an employee to a higher job rank; not advertise a product or encourage an idea
polysemy_resolution_table.take off: a career suddenly becoming successful; not remove clothing or aircraft leaving ground
polysemy_resolution_table.apply: submit a job application; not apply a substance or use a rule
polysemy_resolution_table.fire / fired: dismiss someone from employment; not flames, shooting, or firing a weapon
polysemy_resolution_table.lay off / laid off / made redundant: lose employment through an employer's staffing reduction; distinct from resignation or misconduct dismissal
polysemy_resolution_table.quit / resign / step down: leave a job voluntarily, with step down emphasizing departure from a senior role
polysemy_resolution_table.take on someone / take someone on: hire or add a person to a work team, selected by the Hiring and leaving group; not fight or compete
polysemy_resolution_table.lead / manage / project / task: workplace direction, coordination, planned work, and assigned work respectively; not a metal, shadow, film projection, or school assignment
polysemy_resolution_table.train: teach a coworker the skills for their job; not a railway vehicle or athletic conditioning
polysemy_resolution_table.give and take: mutual compromise and cooperation between colleagues; not literal exchange of objects
polysemy_resolution_table.go the extra mile: make additional effort at work; not travel an extra road distance
polysemy_resolution_table.have your hands full / snowed under / up: workload idioms showing a person overwhelmed by work, not literal snow or immersion

sibling_contrasts.career progression: ladder entry, career path, dead end, getting ahead, holding a role, promotion, setting sights, stepping down, and a career taking off must use different spatial metaphors.
sibling_contrasts.employment separation: fire/fired shows employer dismissal; lay off/laid off/made redundant shows role reduction; quit/resign/step down shows voluntary departure.
sibling_contrasts.overload: hands full emphasizes occupied hands; snowed under shows work papers piling over a seated worker; up to your ears and up to your eyeballs use different paper-height cues.
sibling_contrasts.take on variants: both use the employment sense, but vary camera emphasis: employer selecting a candidate versus candidate being welcomed into a team.

art_direction: Constructive editorial scenes with volumetric people and props, warm paper, navy ink, compact cool-blue office details, and only icon-like non-letter marks. No text, letters, or numerals in SVG artwork.
